full_judgment: 16. We have already affirmed the finding of the Court of appeal below that the plaintiffs have proved their long possession in the suit land on the basis of their purchase vide exhibits 1 series, and defendant No. 1 failed to prove his possession in any part of the suit land. On 6-7-91 defendant No.1 instituted Title Suit No. 27 of 1991 against proforma defendant No. 2, Md Haris only for declaration of his title in the entire land appertaining to RS Khatian No. 604 including the suit land by way of a lease. Said RS Khatian appears to have recorded the name of Md Haris as Korsha raiyat under the rent receiver, Usha Rani. According to the list of rent receivers of the area at the relevant time as printed at page 14 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 by the Dhaka Law Reports, Second Edition, such Korsha raiyot had no rent receiving interest. If it is so, such Korsha raiyot had no right under law to create any sub-tenancy in respect of said land. The case of the defendant No.1 that he took lease of the suit land from proforma defendant No. 2, therefore, falls through as a hoax. Neither in this suit nor in the earlier suit, he could say definitely when he actually took lease. He just produced a piece of paper dated 5-1-55 to evidence an admission of proforma defendant No. 2 as to lease, which he did not take any step to prove. Dr Rafiqur Rahman has submitted that in 1955 no one could validly lease out any land. It may also be mentioned that the defendant No. 1 did not say a word about such admission of proforma defendant No. 2 in his earlier suit. Similarly, he got marked exhibit 'Kha' which appears to be a counterfoil of a rent receipt, which was also not proved.
